newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet seeks LaGuardia route - report.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet seeks LaGuardia route - report.

text.p: ValuJet Airlines has asked the Department of Transportation for special clearance to serve New York City's LaGuardia Airport because Delta Air Lines' dominance has led to high fares on the route, a newspaper reported on Wednesday.

The Atlanta-based discount airline has asked the DOT for an exemption to allow it to begin service between Hartsfield International Airport and LaGuardia, the Atlanta Journal- Constitution reported on Wednesday.

A DOT spokesman said the request was under review, the report said. The newspaper quoted ValuJet spokeswoman Marcia Scott as saying the company was making its request because of Delta Air Lines' "excessive market dominance" which had led to "unreasonably high fares" between Atlanta and LaGuardia.
ValuJet briefly operated flights to LaGuardia in the spring of 1996, before the airline was grounded following the crash of Flight 592 in the Florida Everglades.
